title: The cube that flips

data.source: Model dwell times from the R4 rotor, compared with published summary statistics for bistable perception (Borsellino 1972; Zhou 2004; Brascamp 2005; Cao 2016). No raw data.
data.licence: published summary statistics, cited; no data copied

prediction: A fixed CV of 0 or 0.159 fails against the published 0.6; a noisy phase-to-threshold rotor tuned to CV 0.6 gives skewness three times the CV, not the published two; and 300 dwell times are enough to tell those shapes apart.
baseline: The gamma distribution with shape about 2.8, the usual description of dwell times.
why: The predictions held, and they are bad news for the model: the fixed-CV readings are far from the published spread, and the tunable rotor has the wrong skewness. A flip is a first-passage event, as the field already says, but this smooth phase-to-threshold form gives the wrong shape.
